phases.label: Program
phases.who: owner / client: idea, site sketch, brief + rules answers
phases.next_steps: python tools/run_task.py {CODE}   (P1 site … P7 QC; the user answers P2 brief and P3 rules)

phases.label: Plan/Design
phases.who: architect: answers scope questions, adds design inputs, issues the brief
phases.next_steps: python tools/run_task.py {SUB}   (one brief per floor, made by tools/from_program.py; the architect answers S3 scope)

phases.label: Build
phases.who: modeler: picks the room, adds specs / vendor data, signs off QA
phases.next_steps: roombrief.json is in place, so S1–S2 (deck intake) are skipped: start at S3_GEOMETRY (see STAGES.json and AGENTS.md)

skip_when_bridged.S1_INTAKE: roombrief.json came from Plan/Design (no deck intake)

phases.label: Present
phases.who: presenter: picks stills / walkthrough / report, final client acceptance
phases.next_steps: python tools/run_task.py {SUB}   (S0 drafts scope.json; blend_path = the bridged .blend under the work dir input/)

rules: Shared = R2 Projects/{CODE}/ (outputs.keep of each phase + the manifest + each phase's packed state). Private = local projects/{CODE}/inputs/ and the work dir; they never leave the machine unless `project.py share` is run for a file.

share_inputs: generated inputs a phase cannot run without (e.g. Plan/Design's inputs/plan.canvas.json, made from the program's plan_trace) travel in the packed state; user uploads under inputs/ stay private.
A phase can be handed over only when every task in its TASKS.csv is done or skipped (or --force with a reason, which is recorded).
The next person runs `project.py resume {CODE}`: it pulls the manifest, then either restores the phase they continue (state.json) or creates it from the previous phase's published outputs (bridge).

Roles: project.json members {name: role}. Only a member whose role is in the phase's `roles` may save, hand over, resume or share in that phase; the creator is owner. Names are self-declared (--by) until the app signs requests — see README.
codes: Each phase records the project codes it produced (program: [CODE]; plan: one per floor, e.g. CODE_GF, CODE_FF). The next phase makes one project per upstream code ({UP}), with the same code ({SUB} = {UP}).

targets.@work/: the phase project's work dir (outside public/)

canvas: Projects/{CODE}/canvas/current.json — ONE packed multi-level canvas per project (tools/canvas_store.py); revisions in canvas/revs/, log in canvas/index.json
qa: Projects/{CODE}/qa/<phase>/<SUB>/ — the files holding the user's answers, copied at every save/handover

roles.owner: every phase; adds and removes members
